annotation.title_clean: Gender Stereotyping of Robotic Systems in Eldercare: An Exploratory Analysis of Ethical Problems and Possible Solutions
annotation.title_en: Gender Stereotyping of Robotic Systems in Eldercare: An Exploratory Analysis of Ethical Problems and Possible Solutions
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Weßel, M.; Ellerich-Groppe, N.; Schweda, M.
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed ethical analysis of gender stereotyping in eldercare robots. Using a principlist framework (autonomy, care, justice), it maps moral problems and discusses three design strategies: explanation, neutralization and queering. It concludes that gender-fluid robots merit further ethical, social and technological study.
key_provisions_or_claims: Gender cues in robots (morphology, voice, name, behaviour) trigger stereotyped perceptions in human-robot interaction.
Stereotyped care robots may conflict with autonomy, care and justice in pluralistic societies.
Three strategies are proposed: explanation, neutralization and queering of care robots.
Gender-neutral voices and bodies are often still perceived as male.
The idea of a gender-fluid robot deserves closer ethical and technological examination.
